points.text: Theory covers continuous compact targets; molecules include discrete types, so guarantee does not apply.
Conditional independence assumption behind Eq. 9/11 unrealistic for topology and binding.
Assumes experts aligned at a shared time t.
Vina weak proxy; no synthesizability, geometry, diversity or scaffold-retention metrics.
No broader-impact or dual-use statement.
Inference cost grows with experts; no quality-vs-cost analysis.
Gains not attributed to path validity; bump acts as extra guidance.
'Provably guarantees'/'unbiased' hold only for ideal scores, continuous variables, infinite particles.
Theorem B.2 lacks the coordinate index of Theorem 2.2.
Collapse prevalence counted over arbitrary schedule triples, not real expert combinations.
Molecular benchmarks favourable by design: weak binders, clamped baselines, DiffSBDD-generated set.
Small n and no confidence intervals for tiny margins.
No scaffold-retention metric.
'More than 5x' holds only against FKC.
Table 1 marks FKC unable to use negative exponents, yet it is run so.
Inconsistencies: omega threshold and initial variance of experts.
Impossible mean and std values in Tables 2 and 3.
Promotional, overstated wording beyond idealized theory and small experiments.
Key results relegated to appendix; Discussion holds main results; duplicate table rows.
Image benchmark far from SOTA yet framed as general paradigm.
Molecular benchmark only 9 pairs; no variance in Tables 3-4.
No code link or reproducibility statement.
Author names in correspondence line and acknowledgments break anonymity.
Table C.1 labels and figure reference style.
Positioning vs FKC thin; Table 1 inconsistent; time-varying exponents possibly incremental.
Criterion elementary, tail-only, ideal densities; finite-sampler effect not shown.
Theorem 2.2 per-coordinate statement not what Theorem B.2 proves.
Time alignment of experts assumed; no SNR-matched composition baseline.
Related work on composition and SMC-for-diffusion brief; references missing.
Causal claim not isolated: bump adds guidance; invalid paths sometimes fine.
Molecular evaluation small with no variance; tiny differences overinterpreted.
Specialized-model comparison not like-for-like: clamped poses, set from ACE expert.
Scaffold retention, size, QED/SA and diversity not reported.
B and ESS threshold selected on reported benchmark; only best omega shown.
Impossible mean in Table 3 and std in Table 2.
'>5x' error reduction only versus FKC.
No code; resampling counts unreported; timing across different GPUs.
Minor inconsistencies: labels, omega threshold, variance, table order.
Origin of ratio-of-densities problem and 'experts' not explained.
Feynman-Kac Correctors lack explicit mathematical formulation.
Significance of Marginal Path Collapse not convincing.
Experimental design unreasonable or inadequately described.
Minor notation issues and extra periods.
Heavy notation; Theorem 2.3 unclear; pseudo-code needed.
How to choose bump coefficient B unexplained.
Minor typos.
Which tasks fit ratio-of-densities framework not shown mathematically; relevance unclear.
Appendix proof errors: incomplete proofs, wrong counterexample, support contradiction.
Undefined symbols, duplicate wording, missing references.
Weak evidence collapse occurs in practice; synthetic setups adversarially designed.
Molecular gains may come from tuning rather than collapse; not measured.

P.summary: Guarantee scope overstated beyond ideal continuous setting.
Expert time alignment assumed; no SNR-matched baseline.
Molecular quality metrics (scaffold retention, QED, diversity) missing.
Gains not attributed to path validity vs extra guidance.
Molecular benchmark favourable; baselines not like-for-like.
Positioning vs FKC thin; Table 1 inconsistent.
Paper structure relegates key results to appendix.
Criterion mathematically light; finite-sample effect unshown.

Q.summary: Ratio-of-densities framing and use cases not explained.
Practical occurrence/significance of collapse weakly evidenced.
Choice of bump coefficient B unexplained.
Errors and gaps in appendix proofs.
Molecular gains not attributed to collapse mitigation.
